devices.name: Polysyndeton
devices.definition: Conjunctions (“and … and …”) piled up to slow the pace and weight every item.

occurrences.note: and all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him
and he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name

devices.name: Anthropopatheia
devices.definition: Ascribing to God human feelings, parts, or actions, by way of condescension to us.

devices.name: Ellipsis
devices.definition: A word or words deliberately left out, to be supplied by the reader — compression and force.

devices.name: Metonymy
devices.definition: Naming something by a word closely associated with it — cause for effect, container for contents, author for writings.

occurrences.note: To strengthen the face is put for boldness or impudence

devices.name: Synecdoche
devices.definition: Substituting a part for the whole, or the whole for a part (“all the world”; “flesh and blood”).

occurrences.note: " And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake ": i.e., all to whom the prophecy refers

devices.name: Polyptoton
devices.definition: Repetition of the same root word in different inflections (“dying you shall die”).

occurrences.note: " God of gods": i.e., the great, living, or true God. The most mighty God
" The Prince of princes": i.e., the most powerful Prince
" A mighty King shall stand up that shall rule with a great rule "; i.e., have a vast dominion
" He shall certainly come." Hebrew, coming he shall come

devices.name: Idiom
devices.definition: A peculiar usage of the Hebrew or Greek that does not carry its literal force — an idiom to be rendered by its sense, not word for word.

devices.name: Climax
devices.definition: A chain in which the end of each step becomes the start of the next, building to a peak.

devices.name: Enigma
devices.definition: A dark saying — a truth wrapped in obscure or riddling terms.

devices.name: Heterosis
devices.definition: Exchange of one grammatical form for another — of tense, number, person, degree, or mood (e.g. a future used for a command).

occurrences.note: "This is the dream; and we (i.e., I) will tell the interpretation thereof."

devices.name: Paronomasia (wordplay)
devices.definition: A play on words that sound alike but differ in sense — pun, rhyme, near-repetition.

devices.name: Rhetorical question
devices.definition: A question asked for effect, not for an answer — to affirm, deny, or provoke thought.

occurrences.note: and many examples in the prophecy of Malachi. 12. In Prohibitions. " Why should I be deprived also of you both in one day ? "

devices.name: Synonymia
devices.definition: Amassing synonyms — words of like meaning — to enforce and enlarge a point.

devices.name: Anabasis
devices.definition: A gradual ascent — a series that mounts, clause by clause, to a high point.

devices.name: Aposiopesis
devices.definition: A sentence broken off unfinished, as if the speaker cannot or will not go on.

devices.name: Gnome (quotation)
devices.definition: A quotation or proverbial maxim woven in — a pithy saying cited for authority or point.

devices.name: Hendiadys
devices.definition: One idea expressed by two words joined with “and,” the second really qualifying the first.

occurrences.note: " It cast down some of the host and of the stars ": i.e., of the starry host. Only one thing, not two

devices.name: Hendiatris
devices.definition: One idea expressed by three words joined with “and” (“the way, the truth, and the life”).

occurrences.note: " All the people, the nations, and the languages fell down and worshipped the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up." Now " languages " do not fall down; neither do they worship; Th

devices.name: Hyperbaton
devices.definition: Words wrenched out of their natural order, throwing weight onto the displaced word.

devices.name: Hyperbole
devices.definition: Deliberate exaggeration, not meant literally, that drives a point home vividly.

occurrences.note: " Gabriel... being caused to fly swiftly." Lit. (see marg,), with weariness: i.e., with such swiftness as to cause weariness

devices.name: Parallelism
devices.definition: Successive lines echo one another in structure — saying the same thing twice, or balancing matched clauses.

occurrences.note: a I Severity (" Whom he would he slew "). b I Favour (" and whom he would he kept alive "), b I Favour (" and whom he would he set up "). a I Severity (" and whom he would he put down "

devices.name: Paregmenon
devices.definition: Words from the same root set near one another (a figure of derivation).

devices.name: Paroemia (proverb)
devices.definition: A proverb — a wayside-saying in common use, cited or coined.

devices.name: Personification
devices.definition: Giving human traits, action, or speech to something impersonal or abstract.

occurrences.note: " This great image... stood before thee." 86S

devices.name: Pleonasm
devices.definition: A deliberate redundancy — more words than strictly needed — to underline or solemnise.

occurrences.note: " And some to shame and everlasting contempt."
